_readme: Single source of truth for the whole Howdy deployment.
Edit this file, re-run deploy.sh, and the app picks up the changes.
You can add a module or a trusted source domain here WITHOUT touching Python.
Secrets never live here — they are generated into /etc/howdy/secrets/ by deploy.sh.

app.name: Howdy
app.tagline: Your companion for life in Australia
app.description: Verified-source guidance for international students and new migrants in Australia. Guidance, not legal advice.
app.mission: Be the first point of contact for every international student and new migrant in Australia — accurate, warm, cited, and always pointing to the right registered expert when the question is bigger than general information.
app.north_star: Brisbane 2032 — the official digital companion for international arrivals.

hosting._comment: Sizing hints for deploy.sh. Cheapest first.

free.target: Oracle Cloud Always Free — ARM Ampere
free.note: Free tier was halved to 2 OCPU / 12 GB in June 2026. Stay at or under or the instance gets terminated.

beta.note: Paid, small, reliable. Right for a public beta.

launch.note: Australian data residency. Required by most university procurement.

_alternatives.claude-haiku-4-5: ~60% cheaper. Worth a blind quality test before launch.
_alternatives.claude-opus-4-8: Higher ceiling, ~2x cost. Overkill for knowledge-base-grounded answers.

web_search._note: Live search for volatile facts (wage rates, fees, dates). HARD-RESTRICTED to the same trusted domains as citation verification — Claude physically cannot search anything else.
search_when: the answer depends on a current dollar figure, rate, fee or threshold
the answer depends on a date, deadline or 'as of' year
the user asks what the rule is 'now' or 'currently'
the knowledge base has no entry for the topic
web_search._cost_note: Each search adds cost. max_uses_per_answer caps it. Set enabled=false to run knowledge-base-only.

privacy._note: 0 retention days means 'keep until the user deletes it'. Guest and incognito write nothing at all.

sources._note: Kip may ONLY cite these. Verified server-side after every reply; anything else is stripped.

housing_search._note: Kip never invents listings. It builds live search URLs on these platforms.

legal.disclaimer: Kip provides general information sourced from official Australian government websites. It is not legal, migration, tax or financial advice, and is not a substitute for a registered professional.
legal._critical: Under the Migration Act 1958, giving immigration assistance without registration is a criminal offence. Kip must only ever give GENERAL information and refer individual matters to a MARA-registered agent. Have a registered agent review app/prompt.py and knowledge/base.json before launch.

cities._note: From the founder platform document. Weekly budgets are share-accommodation estimates in AUD; rent ranges are share-room. Verify against the live source before quoting to a student. Concession ENTITLEMENT is deliberately not stated here — it differs by state and visa, and asserting it is how a student ends up with a fare-evasion fine. See the discounts section.

discounts._note: LINK, NEVER LIST — the same rule as housing. Kip must not invent a discount, a percentage or an offer. This section supplies the authoritative starting point for the student's own state; the live figure and the current eligibility rule are searched, never recalled.
discounts._url_policy: URLs here are site roots on purpose. Deep concession pages get restructured every year and a dead link is worse for a student than one extra click. `find` is the phrase Kip searches on that domain to reach the exact current page.
discounts.eligibility_caution: International students are NOT automatically entitled to a public transport concession in every Australian state, and the rules differ by state and by visa. Travelling on a concession fare you are not entitled to is fare evasion and carries a fine. Always check the state authority's own page before buying or tapping a concession fare.

pricing._note: No trial. Nothing anywhere in the product may offer or mention a free trial.
pricing._positioning: The paid tier is NOT a discount list. UNiDAYS and Student Beans are free and better resourced at aggregating offers than we will ever be — charging for that is a losing position at any price. What a student cannot get elsewhere, and what is genuinely worth money, is not missing a deadline. Visa expiry, OSHC lapse, lease end, tax deadline. Missing one of those is the highest-stakes thing in their year here.

free.name: Free
free.includes: Every question about living in Australia — visas, work, tax, housing, health, safety, rights, culture, and the RULES around concessions.
free._why_rules_are_free: Concession eligibility is a safety answer, not a deal. Getting it wrong is a fare-evasion fine, so it can never sit behind a paywall.

plus.name: Kip Plus
plus._name_note: Was 'Student Deals'. Renamed because deals are a feature of this tier, not the reason to buy it. One-line change if you prefer the old name.
plus._annual_note: $79/year is $6.58/month effective. Students think in semesters and years, not months, and annual halves churn.
plus._live_note: DO NOT charge $10 until the deadline keeper ships. Doubling the price with the same features drops conversion further than the price rises — $5 at 2% and $10 at 1% are identical revenue. Flip this to true the day the keeper is live.

features.name: Deadline keeper
features.what: Visa expiry, OSHC renewal, lease end, tax deadline, enrolment dates — tracked, with reminders before they matter.
features.why: The single strongest reason to pay. Missing a visa expiry is catastrophic, and it costs us a scheduled job and a notification — no model call at all.

features.what: Your CoE, lease, payslips and insurance, encrypted, findable when an agent or employer asks for them.

features.what: Turn any answer into a PDF with its sources, to show a landlord, employer or agent.

features.name: Unlimited live checks

features.why: The one feature that maps directly to what it costs us to serve.

quotas._note: Free-tier allowances. Sliding windows, not calendar days — a calendar reset invites asking the daily cap at 23:59 and again at 00:01, and dumps everyone on the server at midnight. Rolling means the answer is always 'you can ask again in N hours', which is also easier to say kindly.
quotas._exempt_note: SAFETY IS NEVER RATIONED. A student asking about family violence, an underpaying employer or a mental health crisis must never meet a paywall or a counter. These modules are not counted and cannot be blocked, at any tier, including signed out.

guest.label: Signed out
guest._why: Enough to prove Kip is useful before asking for anything. The nudge to sign in comes after it has helped, not before.
guest._shared_ip_note: Guests are counted by hashed IP, so a campus behind one NAT shares this allowance. That is a known limit of not writing anything down for signed-out users, and it is the right trade: the fix is signing in, which is free.

free.label: Free account
free._why: A real free user asks about 30 questions a MONTH — roughly one a day. 15/day is fifteen times that, so it never touches normal use, and it holds a single free account to about $4.35/month even if someone sits at the ceiling every day. The earlier 25/day worked out at $7/month per abuser, which is more than the paid tier costs.

deals.label: Student Deals
deals._why: Sized as an abuse ceiling, not a margin guarantee. Realistic use — 5 questions a day, 2 of them searched — is about $1.62/month against the $5 price. Someone hitting this cap every single day for a month would cost ~$10.70, which is a deliberate ~2x exposure on the rare heavy user rather than caps mean enough to spoil normal use.

quotas._cost_basis: Measured 2026-08-19: 0.43c a library answer, 2.04c when it searches. See app/costs.py.

answer_cache._note: Serving a repeated question from the last good answer. The single biggest cost lever we have — see `python -m app.scale 500000 --levers`. Students ask the same things; 'how do I apply for a TFN' does not have 50,000 different answers.
answer_cache._ttl_note: Two days for an answer that came from the library, fifteen minutes for one that needed a live search. Whether it searched is the volatility signal — if a figure can move, we do not serve it from memory for long.
answer_cache._never_note: A crisis answer is generated fresh, in that student's own words, every time. Same reasoning as exempting them from quotas: these are the moments the product exists for and they are never optimised.
